title: Streamline RAG authoring: interactive example gallery and browser sandbox
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add an interactive RAG example gallery with runnable browser sandbox, include telemetry probes and lightweight devcontainer for local playtesting; improves onboarding for engineers and product teams; no breaking API changes.
description: Motivation: engineers repeatedly asked for a compact, shareable set of end-to-end RAG examples that can be executed in a browser without heavyweight infra. This PR adds an interactive example gallery that surfaces curated authoring patterns (streaming, tool-calling, structured outputs) and a minimal browser sandbox that runs against the hosted Redwood demo runtime. Goals: 1) lower onboarding time for new RAG authors, 2) provide runnable reference patterns for tool-calling and telemetry, 3) make examples embeddable in docs pages. Summary of changes: gallery page with example cards and live iframe sandboxes; three new runnable examples (basic RAG, tool-calling with a simulated webhook, structured-output + schema validation); lightweight browser sandbox assets (HTML/JS/CSS) that proxy to a demo token endpoint; a tiny devcontainer for local iteration; a build script that compiles the gallery index and validates example manifests; added telemetry probes to sample examples so we can collect SDK usage and latency distributions. Security notes: sandbox uses a short-lived demo token and origin restrictions; no secret material checked in. Rollout plan: merged to main behind the docs feature flag, staged to the docs beta site for one week before public promotion. Checklist: ensure demo tokens rotated and disabled in CI; add short README for maintainers; confirm telemetry events match telemetry spec; add a quick smoke test to docs CI. Related work: follows ENG-1423 and links to previous authoring guides in PM-78.
